races.name: CopyBet And Worcester Here All Year Novices' Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Feet On The Ground
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits if strong pace develops, but quick turnaround from encouraging debut third may catch her fresh
runners_data.comment: Modest hurdler but a pointing background bodes well for this switch to fences
runners_data.spotlight: No threat to easy winner Beorma when third of five on chasing debut here (2m, good) two weeks ago but that run was still quite encouraging, and she might be better suited by this longer trip; won't mind if the ground softens; one to consider.

runners_data.name: Wings On Wheels
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner aided by cheekpieces last time, though longer gap since last run could blunt his sharpness
runners_data.comment: Still unexposed under rules but needs improvement over this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Still unexposed under rules and was seemingly aided by new cheekpieces when second of four at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) in March; that form isn't anything to get excited about, though, and he was well held when third at Perth (2m4f, good to soft) last month; now tries a visor; forecast rain probably not ideal.

runners_data.name: Best Mate Dave
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning to handicap company after hunter chase, but 5lb claimer's inexperience is a concern in tactical race
runners_data.spotlight: Not beaten far when last of four in Warwick hunter chase (3m, good) last month but managed only fifth of seven in a subsequent point; back in a handicap chase for stable debut; quite tricky to weigh up at the moment; seems best suited by good ground.

runners_data.name: Dynamite Defense
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner switching from hurdles to fences for new stable, lowest weight offers some compensation
runners_data.comment: Won over 1m on the Flat in Ireland in 2024; no joy since and makes debut for new yard.
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in two low-grade AW handicaps for Olly Murphy in February/March but was last of six when back over hurdles here (2m, good) for new stable last month and is not bred for chasing.

runners_data.name: Les's Destiny Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up style needs strong gallop, returning from 37-day break after disappointing last run
runners_data.comment: Had wind surgery prior to resurgent effort over C&D last time; respected off same mark
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner; 0-6 over hurdles and needs to bounce back from a poor run but his third of 14 at Ffos Las (3m, good to soft) in April was a good effort; drops back in trip and sports first-time cheekpieces on chasing debut; could have a say if back on song.

runners_data.name: Beorma
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in red-hot form with four wins in fortnight, but 7lb penalty and 2-day turnaround are potential negatives
runners_data.comment: Fast-improving mare who has collected three easy wins in the last 12 days
runners_data.spotlight: Fast-improving mare who has been on the rampage over the last fortnight, winning two 2m chases and two hurdles (2m4f/2m) on good ground; carries 7lb penalty for Tuesday's success over fences at Southwell but did that pretty easily; obvious contender, providing she's not derailed by significant rain.

runners_data.name: Rockvale
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with clear second last time to next-time-out winner, racing off same mark with strong each-way claims
runners_data.comment: Yet to make the frame in six starts under rules, sixth at Bangor last month
runners_data.spotlight: 0-10 under all codes but was clear second to a next-time-out winner over fences at Uttoxeter (2m5f, good) last month and has each-way claims at least off same mark here; placed in Irish points on soft ground.

runners_data.name: Miss Pearl
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare making chasing debut for new stable, longer trip may suit better than previous efforts
runners_data.comment: She finished well behind over hurdles last week after a layoff
runners_data.spotlight: Still a maiden after 16 runs but hasn't been with current stable long and wasn't beaten far when fourth of six on chasing debut at Ffos Las (3m, good to soft) three weeks ago; may benefit from this drop back in trip and has the services of Sean Bowen; worth a second look.

runners_data.name: Emberscombe
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with point wins but poor Rules record, 7lb claimer adds uncertainty to tactical approach
runners_data.spotlight: Won two four-runner points this spring but has poor record under rules (0-14) and makes only limited appeal here.

runners_data.name: Kings Order
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with poor hurdles record but showed point ability, long absence since March is major negative
runners_data.spotlight: Unplaced all six hurdle runs, most recently when beaten about 28l in Chepstow handicap (2m, good to soft) in March, but his Irish point second last spring offers a ray of hope on this chasing debut.

races.paceDynamic: Beorma will likely lead or share the early pace with Emberscombe, though Beorma's prominent style and current form streak suggests she'll control proceedings. With limited early pace pressure from mostly hold-up horses, Beorma can dictate a steady gallop that suits her improving profile. The lack of confirmed front-runners means the pace will be manageable rather than breakneck, allowing patient types to stay in touch. This controlled tempo strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed to position close to the pace, rather than pure hold-up horses who need a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beorma Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma gets an uncontested lead and dictates her own fractions
scenarios.body: Her recent winning streak continues as she can time her effort perfectly without pace pressure. The lack of early speed allows her to conserve energy for a decisive move.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes surprisingly strong with multiple horses going forward
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop brings stamina into play and allows the patient types to close strongly. Hold-up specialists can pick off the pace-setters in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Emberscombe or another runner challenges Beorma for the lead early
scenarios.body: The increased pace pressure creates gaps for horses with tactical speed to exploit. Those able to track the leaders without getting involved in the battle benefit most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse Of Favourites
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma fails to handle her penalty or the quick turnaround tells
scenarios.body: The race opens up for the outsiders with less exposed profiles to capitalise. Rockvale's recent second or Emberscombe's point form could prove decisive.

watchPoints.text: Beorma could be vulnerable to the 7lb penalty combined with her incredibly quick turnaround of just two days
Watch how aggressively Emberscombe or any other runner goes forward early as this will determine if Beorma gets an easy lead
Monitor if Wings On Wheels or Rockvale can get into contention turning for home as both have shown improved recent form
Check if any of the hold-up horses can get close enough in the straight as most need the pace to collapse late
Best Mate Dave's 5lb claiming jockey could make tactical errors in what may become a messy finish

races.name: CopyBet Proudly Backs UK Horse Racing Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Excello
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Henderson with class edge, 62 days off but strong Aintree third suggests retained ability
runners_data.spotlight: Now 4lb lower than when creditable third of 17 over the big Aintree fences (2m5f, good to soft) in November but his subsequent form has been underwhelming; drops in grade here but still needs to up his game and has presumably been overlooked by Nico de Boinville; seems versatile ground-wise.

runners_data.name: Ideal Des Bordes
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in blinkers, strong Newbury second suggests return to form for Henderson stable
runners_data.spotlight: Had very mixed record in 2025 but was creditable second at Newbury (3m2f, good; second run in blinkers) on latest outing in December and has strong claims if in similar form here; well suited by good to soft ground and was a point winner on yielding to soft.

runners_data.name: Samuel Spade
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who lacked fluency on chase debut 14 days ago but showed enough promise for improvement
runners_data.comment: Quiet last season but too well handicapped to dismiss on chasing debut
runners_data.spotlight: Lacked fluency and was ultimately well beaten over C&D (good) on chasing debut a fortnight ago, after a layoff, but significant positives can still be drawn from that performance and he ought to cope better than some of these if the ground softens; can be dangerous if in a better rhythm today.

runners_data.name: Peaky Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying top weight, respectable Uttoxeter third indicates return to form for new stable
runners_data.comment: Below form during light campaign last season but not written off just yet
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointing for new stable last season but appreciated the ease in grade when respectable third of six in quite valuable contest at Uttoxeter (3m, good) last month and won't mind what the weather does here; contender if able to build on that recent effort.

runners_data.name: Stumps Or Slips
runners_data.note: Hunter chase specialist with excellent April form, amateur jockey claims valuable 3lbs
runners_data.comment: Proved stamina for 3m with ease at Exeter latest (good) and still on the up; big player.
runners_data.spotlight: In excellent form in hunter chases in April, winning twice in good style on good ground (3m/2m7f); can't be ruled out after those exploits but faces tougher assignment on this handicap return and probably won't be favoured by the forecast rain.

runners_data.name: Disco Davis
runners_data.note: Front-to-hold-up convert who ran well from front on stable debut, low weight advantage significant
runners_data.comment: 2m hurdle winner; changed hands for 1,000gns after selling hurdle defeat; watching brief.
runners_data.spotlight: Very inconsistent for Dan Skelton last season but ran well from the front when third here (2m4f, good) on stable debut three weeks ago and won't mind if the ground is much slower today (has won on heavy); unexposed over this sort of trip; a possible if in the right mood again.

runners_data.name: Presentandcounting
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader and good ground specialist, 36 days freshened and back to favorable mark
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground specialist with nine chase wins on his CV; returned from break with two respectable runs this spring and has edged his way back down to a good mark but the forecast rain is the obvious worry.

runners_data.name: Grand Clermont
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for in-form Pipe stable, impressive Uttoxeter win suggests ready for step up
runners_data.comment: Ex-French where all his winning was on heavy ground; tailed off on British debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won seven chases (most on heavy ground) when based in France and came good for David Pipe at the second attempt, with wide-margin success at Uttoxeter (3m, good) last month; up 10lb in higher-grade race here but still commands respect.

runners_data.name: My Bobby Dazzler
runners_data.note: Prominent type in good spring form, 17 days since last run keeps him match-fit
runners_data.spotlight: Ended last season in good form, winning at Hereford (3m1f, soft) before good second at Haydock (3m1f, good), and ran quite a bit better than eventual 20l defeat suggests when fourth in Cartmel marathon (3m5f, good) last month; no surprise if he features here.

runners_data.name: Bagheera Ginge
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner wearing first-time visor, 25 days since confidence-boosting Stratford win
runners_data.comment: Off since poor run in October and still on fairly tough mark; headgear switched
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who returned from seven-month break with 7l win in first-time visor at Stratford (2m6f, good to firm) last month; only 4lb higher here but the market principals in that race disappointed and the form is of questionable value; raced mainly on good ground but has won on good to soft and been placed on soft.

races.paceDynamic: Bagheera Ginge and Presentandcounting are confirmed front-runners who will contest the early pace over this extended trip at Worcester. Both are proven pace-setters with strong good ground form, so expect an honest gallop from flag to finish with little respite in the middle section. The demanding 2m7f distance and sustained pace will create a stern test of stamina. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can conserve energy early and produce late finishing kicks when the pace-setters tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominant
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves too strong and both front-runners tire
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will set up perfectly for closers like Excello, Samuel Spade and Peaky Boy who can pick off tired leaders. Henderson's proven big-race ability with Excello and the class drop makes this the most likely outcome.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Ideal Des Bordes or Grand Clermont can track the pace without over-racing
scenarios.body: These horses can sit close enough to strike when the leaders weaken but avoid the energy-sapping front-running duties. Both have strong recent form and the tactical speed to capitalize when the race develops.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters can establish a decisive early advantage
scenarios.body: Presentandcounting's good ground specialist status or Bagheera Ginge's recent confidence boost could see one skip clear. The 12-year-old experience of Presentandcounting particularly suits this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Collapse Race
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly unsustainable and multiple horses stop
scenarios.body: The combination of 2m7f distance and fierce early pace could see widespread faltering in the final furlong. This would heavily favor the most conservative hold-up horses with proven staying power.

watchPoints.text: Watch Bagheera Ginge and Presentandcounting in the early stages - if both go too fast the pace will collapse
Monitor Samuel Spade's jumping fluency after struggling with his fences on chase debut two weeks ago
Check how Ideal Des Bordes settles in blinkers - previous over-racing issues could resurface under pressure
Watch for Excello's jumping rhythm after 62-day break, as Henderson horses sometimes need time to find their stride
Observe amateur rider Zac Baker's positioning on Stumps Or Slips - tactical awareness crucial in competitive handicap

races.name: CopyBet Royal Ascot Bog From Sunday Mares' NH Flat Race (Conditional/Amateurs) Cat 1 Elim) (GBB)

runners_data.name: Dora's Double
runners_data.spotlight: First foal; dam point winner, out of unraced half-sister to Midlands Grand National winner Russian Trigger; stable has healthy strike-rate in bumpers (12%); market may guide.

runners_data.name: Evenly
runners_data.spotlight: Second foal; dam maiden pointer/well beaten in bumper, half-sister to useful jumper Bobs Law; stable does pretty well in bumpers (12% strike-rate); a possible.

runners_data.name: Honour Me
runners_data.spotlight: £1,000 3yo; ninth foal; half-sister to winners Persian Time (useful hurdle/chase), Restandbethankful (bumper/jumps), Thermusa (hurdle) and Little Jack (bumper); dam maiden; with a good stable; plausible contender.

runners_data.name: Lady Of Tarsus
runners_data.spotlight: Third foal from unraced sister to high-class bumper/hurdle winner Kilcooley; beaten before unseating rider at penultimate fence in heavy-ground Irish point in February; may fare better in this different contest.

runners_data.name: Maximore
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up in two points this year but represents astute Irish stable and is worth a glance in the betting before this rules debut; hood fitted.

runners_data.name: Crack Of Thunder
runners_data.spotlight: 23,000gns yearling; second foal; half-sister to a fair sprinter; dam well-connected 6f winner; not an obvious type for bumpers but represents good Flat stable and has presumably inherited stamina from his sire.

runners_data.name: Eagles Promise
runners_data.spotlight: Fifth foal; dam fair 2m hurdle winner, sister to smart bumper/jumps winner Super Duty and useful jumper Grandads Cottage; one of two newcomers in this field for Tom George (4-22 in bumpers in last five seasons).

runners_data.name: Lucy Glitters
runners_data.spotlight: Ninth foal; half-sister to a point winner; dam bumper/2m5f hurdle winner, half-sister to bumper and 2m6f/3m hurdle winner Smart Mover; one of two newcomers from this stable; wears a hood.

runners_data.name: Matilda Maid
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth foal; half-sister to two point winners; dam unplaced in bumpers, half-sister to stable's Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Coneygree and high-class jumper Carruthers; might be a longer-term prospect.

runners_data.name: Pearl Cove
runners_data.spotlight: Seventh foal; half-sister to low-grade chase winner Eightytwo Team; dam useful hurdler/chaser, half-sister to Flat winner/useful hurdler Dangerously Good; rare bumper runner for the stable.

runners_data.name: Poppieholla
runners_data.spotlight: Third foal; sister to 2m3f hurdle winner Briefly, half-sister to 2m hurdle winner Sammy's Guarantee; dam bumper winner/placed 2m6f hurdle, half-sister to useful bumper/jumps winner Thomas Brown; makes some appeal on pedigree but stable not prolific in bumpers.

runners_data.name: Queens Glance
runners_data.spotlight: First foal; dam low-grade 2m Flat winner, half-sister to stable's fair hurdler I'm A Starman; wears a tongue-tie; other newcomers look more interesting on paper.

runners_data.name: Tottie's Moon
runners_data.spotlight: First foal; dam unplaced in bumper/over hurdles, sister to useful jumper Mac Tottie; wears a tongue-tie; stable does well in bumpers.

runners_data.name: Pearl Knot
runners_data.comment: Yard 21% in bumpers in recent years and she needs watching in market on debut
runners_data.spotlight: Third foal; half-sister to low-grade chase winner Pearl Island; dam 2m6f-3m hurdle winner, sister to 3m-3m5f chase winner Bretney, closely related to useful 2m4f-4m hurdle/chase winner Captain Cattistock; has stout pedigree but stable does well in bumpers (21% strike-rate).

runners_data.name: Unflappable
runners_data.comment: £4,500 3yo; third foal; half-sister to 2m-2m1f chase winner Pure Carbon
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to fairly useful chaser Pure Carbon; made promising debut when clear third of ten under positive ride at Newton Abbot (good) last month and ought to put that experience to good use here.

runners_data.name: Liberty Leader
runners_data.comment: Has fair target to aim at on debut and is best watched unless market suggests otherwise
runners_data.spotlight: Out of a half-sister to smart jumper Libberty Hunter but showed only minor promise when fifth of nine at Bangor (good) last month and needs to take a big step forward here.

races.name: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div I)

runners_data.name: Luckonthemoor
runners_data.note: Unraced newcomer with unknown running style making belated debut at age 8 - market moves essential
runners_data.spotlight: First foal; dam 1m4f AW winner (RPR 76), half-sister to useful jumper Smarty Wild; probably best watched on belated debut.

runners_data.name: Lucky Diamond
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course form advantage but carries unseating baggage from recent bumper
runners_data.comment: Sufficient promise in his second bumper run to believe he'll have a role to play
runners_data.spotlight: Blotted copybook when veering right and unseating rider soon after the start of a recent bumper but the form of his third here last October (good ground) has worked out quite well; could have a say if all goes to plan on hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Premier Tenor
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong recent third over course and distance, benefits from Harry Skelton booking
runners_data.comment: Dam French 2m1f hurdle winner; French 13.5f Flat winner; interesting on stable debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Made winning debut on the Flat in France last October (good to soft); unable to justify favouritism when third (just behind Shamsat) over C&D (good; first-time hood/tongue-tie) three weeks ago but that still goes down as a promising stable/hurdle debut, and he has obvious scope for progress.

runners_data.name: Babs
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who races too freely, 15 days since last run, must settle better to win
runners_data.comment: Won a bumper on debut in October but she's not gone on from that; needs improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Doesn't help herself by tending to race too freely but won good-ground Stratford bumper in the autumn and ran big race in defeat over hurdles at Newton Abbot (2m1f, good) a fortnight ago; should cope if the ground eases; can make her presence felt.

runners_data.name: Drombeg Lad
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with solid course bumper form but facing major fitness test after 284-day layoff
runners_data.spotlight: Went close in good-ground course bumper a year ago and was placed on both hurdling starts last summer, the latter over C&D; has fitness to prove after 284-day absence and ground slower than good would be new to him but he still enters each-way calculations.

runners_data.name: Shamsat
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with consistent placed form in similar events, looks the main pace angle threat
runners_data.spotlight: Won on the Flat in France last year (heavy ground) and has been placed on both British hurdling starts, more recently when second of ten in similar race to this over C&D three weeks ago; likely contender again.

runners_data.name: Trouville
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making hurdles debut off long Flat layoff, 13,000gns purchase suggests ability
runners_data.spotlight: Useful Flat racer who was placed in Class 3 AW handicap (2m; RPR 89) on latest outing last summer; changed hands for 13,000gns in the autumn; has form on good and soft ground; will be dangerous at this level if he takes adequately to hurdling at the first attempt.

runners_data.name: Hollysaway
runners_data.note: Prominent type but badly outclassed, recent wind operation needs to show dramatic improvement
runners_data.comment: 200-1 when tailed off in a novice hurdle for mares at Chepstow in March
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at big odds on both hurdling starts (2m/2m1f); needs subsequent wind op to have made a massive difference.

runners_data.name: Amalfina
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making stable and hurdles debut with fair Flat form at extended distances
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 on the Flat for Karl Burke but showed some fair form at up to 1m5f and seems versatile ground-wise; sold for 7,000gns in the autumn; makes stable/hurdle debut after eight-month break.

runners_data.name: Nightflyer
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with bumper win but inconsistent form since joining current stable
runners_data.comment: Only fourth at Warwick 16 days ago and has much more on his plate here
runners_data.spotlight: Won soft-ground Catterick bumper for Adrian Keatley on debut in January; ran well in only one of three subsequent bumpers for current stable but faced tough task in Aintree festival Grade 2 on latest occasion; should have a future over hurdles and won't mind the forecast rain.

races.paceDynamic: Babs will set the pace from the front with no other confirmed front-runners to apply pressure, creating a sustainable tempo that could become pedestrian. Lucky Diamond and Trouville are likely to track just behind as prominent runners, with the majority of the field including Shamsat, Premier Tenor, and Drombeg Lad settling further back as hold-up horses. The lack of early pace pressure means the race may develop into a tactical affair where the tempo quickens dramatically from 3 furlongs out. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and those with a strong finishing kick who can capitalise on the likely modest early fractions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Babs sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays moderate throughout
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from 3 furlongs out where class and finishing speed decide the outcome. Hold-up horses with proven acceleration benefit most from the tactical nature and ability to produce their best when it matters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Babs maintains control and sees out the trip strongly when the pace lifts
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows Babs to dictate ideal fractions and kick clear when challenged. Front-running tactics prove decisive with prominent racers potentially following home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Babs races too freely early and fades badly in the straight
scenarios.body: The confirmed front-runner's tendency to race keenly backfires under pressure, creating a messy pace that favours versatile types. Those tracking prominently can capitalise on the pace collapse.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Development
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with multiple horses tracking closely
scenarios.body: The race develops into a true test of stamina where proven stayers and those with bumper form excel. Experience over the trip and proven stamina reserves become crucial factors.

watchPoints.text: Babs could race too keenly early and compromise her chance despite having ideal pace scenario
Drombeg Lad faces significant fitness questions after 284 days off despite solid course form
Trouville making hurdles debut off 345-day layoff could need the run despite useful Flat form
Luckonthemoor market moves crucial given complete lack of racecourse experience at age 8
Lucky Diamond's behaviour at the start given recent unseating incident when veering right

races.name: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div II)

runners_data.name: Mystic Wind
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4-year-old from powerful Skelton yard making hurdles debut, unknown quantity but stable stats suggest confidence
runners_data.spotlight: First foal; dam placed 1m3f AQPS Flat/well held only hurdles start, closely related to a French 2m3f chase winner, half-sister to to two French AQPS Flat winners; represents a top stable but it's unnerving to see a hood fitted on debut.

runners_data.name: Fiskardo
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won well on good ground last time, ideal positioned behind Purple Owl with solid recent form
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner last month but others in here did have superior form in that scene
runners_data.spotlight: Led on post to win good-ground Perth bumper in April, after a long layoff, and wasn't discredited when well-held second over hurdles at Ffos Las (2m, good to soft; winner had useful bumper form) last month; probably won't be far away.

runners_data.name: Dancingondiamonds
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the race shape, given wind operation since last disappointing run and trainer has decent strike rate
runners_data.comment: Debut promise in May; gelded since and won't have to improve too much to play major role
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to build upon last spring's quite promising Irish Flat debut when unplaced odds-on favourite in AW maiden in January but was given a wind op soon afterwards and has joined good stable for hurdling career.

runners_data.name: Bacardi Blue
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with poor recent form, 275 days off the track makes this a very tough assignment
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off in Newton Abbot bumper last September and returns to racing under rules after well-held second in two-finisher point last month; look elsewhere.

runners_data.name: Minella Blizzard
runners_data.note: Struggled badly in recent starts including a pull-up, first-time cheekpieces unlikely to transform poor form
runners_data.comment: Out of a well-connected mare but was pulled up on his Irish point debut in April
runners_data.spotlight: Out of a well-connected mare but was pulled up on Irish point debut in April and also struggled in a recent novice hurdle; wears first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Just Call Me Buzz
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who finished strong second over course and distance three weeks ago, may need stronger pace
runners_data.comment: Stayed on into third in a Chepstow maiden on his hurdles debut last month
runners_data.spotlight: Well held when third on hurdling debut in April but displayed improvement and lost out only by a nose when second over C&D (good) three weeks ago; might encounter slower ground today but still a major player.

runners_data.name: Purple Owl
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who gets ideal scenario with no pace pressure, dropping back to 2m from longer trips
runners_data.comment: Tailed off/pulled up in two handicaps on either side of a wind op; capable of better
runners_data.spotlight: Fair form when placed twice in novice company towards end of 2025 (2m, good/soft) but well beaten in two 2m4f handicaps this year; drops back in trip here; needs to get career back on track.

runners_data.name: Kernie d'Airy
runners_data.note: Hold-up style may struggle if Purple Owl dictates slow early fractions, needs race to develop into sprint finish
runners_data.comment: Second at Hereford (2m3f) on hurdle debut in March and can build on that effort here
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced since winning slow-ground French bumper on debut in November 2024 but was second on hurdle debut at Hereford (2m3f, good) in March and might not have been suited by the idiosyncratic track when below that form at Fakenham (2m4f, good) last month; drops back in trip with tongue-tie added here; has a fighting chance.

runners_data.name: Angel Of My Dreams
runners_data.note: Prominent racer but has shown tendency to fade in finish, warning sign for stamina at this trip
runners_data.comment: Won a point bumper on debut but well beaten in both subsequent rules bumpers
runners_data.spotlight: Easily won a point bumper in March 2025 (good to soft) but did not show much in three rules bumpers (remote when second last month); significant improvement required on hurdle debut; tongue-tie removed.

races.paceDynamic: Purple Owl is the only confirmed front runner and will be allowed an uncontested lead from the start. With no other natural pace horses and several hold-up types like Just Call Me Buzz and Kernie d'Airy, Purple Owl can dictate a steady gallop through the early stages. The lack of pace pressure means the tempo will be moderate until the field bunches up approaching the final flight, creating a sprint finish from the last hurdle. This race shape heavily favours front runners and prominent racers who can position close to Purple Owl and avoid traffic problems in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Purple Owl gets an easy lead and finds improvement dropping back to 2m
scenarios.body: Purple Owl dictates throughout and has enough left to repel late challengers up the straight. The lack of early pace pressure allows the leader to save energy for a sustained kick from the last flight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent racers can sit close to Purple Owl and outfinish in the straight
scenarios.body: Fiskardo or Dancingondiamonds track the leader into the straight and use superior fitness or ability to win going away. The moderate early pace suits horses that can position handy and unleash a telling burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Artist Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes very slow and creates a blanket finish from the back
scenarios.body: Just Call Me Buzz or Kernie d'Airy get the perfect setup with a crawling gallop that becomes a sprint from two out. Their ability to quicken late proves decisive when the field comes together in a bunch.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexposed Type Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If Mystic Wind shows significant improvement from the Skelton yard with first-time headgear
scenarios.body: The lightly raced Mystic Wind benefits from the strong stable backing and tactical ride from Harry Skelton. The moderate pace allows the newcomer to travel comfortably before producing an eye-catching finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch Purple Owl's early fractions - if allowed to crawl through the first mile unchallenged, the leader will be very hard to pass
Monitor Just Call Me Buzz's positioning turning for home - needs to be within striking distance despite hold-up style given likely moderate pace
Check how Mystic Wind travels on debut for the Skeltons - any confident riding from Harry Skelton could signal a live outsider
Observe Fiskardo's jumping rhythm early on - needs to stay close to Purple Owl to capitalize on prominent running style
Watch the field's bunching approaching the final flight - if they're still in a line the pace has been too slow for hold-up horses

runners_data.name: Sunray Shadow

runners_data.name: American Mike

runners_data.spotlight: Very smart 3m-winning chaser for Gordon Elliott in 2024/25; also scored over fences for current yard at Perth (3m) in April but beat just one when tried in cheekpieces in 2m4f handicap chase at Uttoxeter 18 days ago; reverts to hurdles off a 7lb lower mark but still has something to prove.

runners_data.name: Shallow River
runners_data.note: Hold-up type fresh after 33-day break for Olly Murphy, but trainer's poor recent record and removed cheekpieces raise questions
runners_data.comment: Won 3m h'cap hurdle at Carlisle in December 2024; not run since; looks stable's 2nd string
runners_data.spotlight: Took a step forward on just his second run for Olly Murphy when landing 3m1f handicap hurdle at Carlisle in October 2024; went without his usual cheekpieces after 17 months off when a never-dangerous sixth in 2m4f Hexham handicap last month; can strip sharper now with headgear refitted.

runners_data.name: Ballintubber Boy
runners_data.note: Natural front runner looked rusty last time but Sam Twiston-Davies can utilise uncontested lead to best advantage over this staying trip
runners_data.comment: Absent since two small-field seconds in October but is 3-3 over C&D; likely contender
runners_data.spotlight: Looked rusty after seven months off when last of seven in 3m1f handicap hurdle at Huntingdon 23 days ago; this fairly useful winning hurdler can take a step forward now.

runners_data.name: Gwennie May Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 173-day layoff which is concerning for fitness, though has class when right
runners_data.comment: Won Grade 2 Rendlesham last February but hasn't matched that form before or since
runners_data.spotlight: A smart 3m-winning hurdler for Dan Skelton in 2024/25; only raced twice for Olly Murphy last season and not seen out since being pulled up in Long Walk Hurdle at Ascot in December; has it to prove starting out for another new yard here.

races.paceDynamic: Ballintubber Boy is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start, with four hold-up horses (Sunray Shadow, American Mike, Shallow River, Gwennie May Boy) tracking behind. The pace will be genuinely run but sustainable as Ballintubber Boy faces no early pressure, allowing him to establish rhythm over this stamina-testing 2m7f trip. With the field bunching behind a lone leader and strong galloping ground, this race sets up perfectly for patient hold-up horses who can produce late kicks. The tactical shape strongly favours closers who can time their challenges from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Ballintubber Boy maintains strong gallop throughout and hold-up horses time runs well
scenarios.body: The sustained tempo will stretch out the field perfectly for late-running types to pick off the leader in the closing stages. Patient tactical rides from Skelton and Bowen will prove decisive as their mounts arrive with finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Ballintubber Boy gets soft fractions and kick clear turning in
scenarios.body: Without early pressure, the leader conserves energy for decisive move approaching two out and holds off late challengers. His class and tactical advantage from the front proves too much for the closers to reel in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If Ballintubber Boy goes too steady early allowing closers to crowd him
scenarios.body: The lack of early tempo means the hold-up horses get into contention too easily and gang up on the leader. Multiple challengers swamp Ballintubber Boy as he has no kick response when pressured.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rustiness Costs Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Ballintubber Boy shows effects of recent poor run and fades late
scenarios.body: The leader's disappointing Huntingdon effort carries over as he weakens significantly in final furlong under pressure. Fresh legs of the patient hold-up horses prove decisive in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Ballintubber Boy may compound poor Huntingdon form if showing similar sluggishness, making him vulnerable to late challenges
Tom Hutsby's inexperience on American Mike could cost in tactical finish as 10lb claimer may struggle with timing of challenge
Shallow River's headgear removal suggests confidence but watch early positioning as he needs to be handy enough to strike
Gwennie May Boy's lengthy absence means fitness is major unknown despite his obvious class credentials
Track Sunray Shadow's position at halfway as Skelton will want him close enough to unleash his proven finishing kick

runners_data.name: Bobbarelli
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who will dictate proceedings but seeking first rules win and may lack finishing kick when challenged

runners_data.spotlight: Dual point winner; still seeking first rules win (0-6); likes to race prominently, weakening on the run-in when last seen over hurdles at Taunton (2m3f, good) in April; went down fighting over fences at Stratford 12 days ago; player.

runners_data.name: Katana
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from long break for new trainer, class horse but fitness major concern after 220 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up over C&D on final start for Nicky Henderson last May, and again on first start for this trainer (6-4 favourite) the following month; badly out of sorts since and remains winless; handicap mark has plummeted accordingly; clear risks attached.

runners_data.name: Western Soldier
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won last time out at Wincanton, ideal style for this race shape and relatively fresh
runners_data.comment: Not much has gone to plan since his quite stylish Wincanton win in November
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Wincanton (1m7f, good; from 2lb lower) last November, but lost his way and unseated in March; stayed on into modest fourth at Hexham (2m; beaten 12l) three weeks ago, though; slightly more needed.

runners_data.name: Son Of Hypnos
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying 7lb claimer, trainer having first runner but horse showed ability in Ireland

runners_data.name: Play Pretend
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won at this course previously, below par recently but tactical style suits race perfectly
runners_data.comment: May have needed his reappearance run at Worcester and has claims if back near best
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner (three ran) last July and beaten a neck over 2m4f here (similar mark) last October; below par in two starts this year, lacking fluency when beaten 36l at Bangor (2m4f, good) latest; a possible on peak form.

runners_data.name: Emerald Time
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer wearing tongue tie, fell when going well last time and could be overpriced
runners_data.comment: Showed ability in bumpers and in his qualifying races; improvement possible in handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in a Warwick bumper and glimpses of ability over hurdles, none more so than when falling two out at Ludlow (2m, soft) in February; lacked the pace to challenge on handicap debut at Aintree (2m1f, good) but still unexposed; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Privilege
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 299-day break, twice runner-up at Newton Abbot but fitness major worry
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win came on the Flat at Tipperary (7.5f) in June 2021; twice runner-up at Newton Abbot (2m3f, good) this time last year; weakened quickly on latest start at Bath last August; isn't impossible, but reasons to oppose.

runners_data.name: Raffles Nobu
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner wearing tongue strap and blinkers, weakened quickly last time but good third two starts ago
runners_data.comment: Sole win was in France in 2023 and he went out like a light at Uttoxeter three weeks ago

runners_data.name: Belcamo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 144-day break, won last time out but in weak contest and now 3lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Broke his duck over jumps at Fakenham (2m, good to soft) in January; that wasn't a particularly strong contest and he has been absent since; now 3lb higher.

runners_data.name: Barafundle Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who jumped left last time, well beaten in all three hurdles starts to date

runners_data.name: Strong As Steel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 165-day break, pulled up three times recently and major fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Best run was in a bumper and he's struggled to find a foothold over hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: 0-11; pulled up in three of his last five runs; returns from six-month break on just his third outing for trainer (also represented by Alex The Great); an easing mark aside, there aren't too many positives.

runners_data.name: Alex The Great
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with headgear change to tongue tie, well beaten over hurdles and needs major improvement
runners_data.comment: Beaten long way in two similar events over 2m at Hereford recently.
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time AW winner (1m6f-2m); well beaten in three spins over hurdles; lowly rated for handicap debut but he needs a spark; stablemate of Strong As Steel.

races.paceDynamic: Bobbarelli will set a sustainable pace from the front with no genuine pace pressure in this 12-runner field. The prominent runners like Katana and Son Of Hypnos will track without applying early pressure, while the large contingent of hold-up horses including Western Soldier, Play Pretend, Emerald Time, Privilege, Raffles Nobu, Belcamo, Barafundle Bay, Strong As Steel and Alex The Great will settle behind. This setup creates a moderate gallop early before the race comes alive from the final flight. The tactical verdict strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late finishing kicks, as the uncontested leader will likely weaken and the patient runners can exploit the modest early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Exploit Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Bobbarelli sets modest fractions and the prominent horses fail to apply pressure turning in
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up horses get perfect conditions to unleash finishing kicks from the back, overwhelming a weakening leader and any prominently-raced horses who lack a change of gear. Western Soldier and Play Pretend benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Katana Kicks From Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Katana travels strongly in second and has enough left to challenge Bobbarelli from the last flight
scenarios.body: The Henderson-trained runner uses his class advantage from an ideal tracking position, while the hold-up horses get caught too far back on ground that may not suit their style perfectly. Son Of Hypnos could also benefit from similar tactics.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Bobbarelli Stays On Gamely
scenarios.trigger: If the leader maintains strong gallop throughout and the pace doesn't collapse as expected
scenarios.body: The dual point winner finally converts over hurdles by dictating terms completely, with his stamina proving superior when challenged by late closers. Western Soldier emerges best of the chasers but cannot quite get there.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely collapses and an unfancied hold-up horse produces an unexpected turn of foot
scenarios.body: One of the longer-priced runners like Emerald Time or Belcamo benefits from a sprint finish that exposes the favourite's limitations. The modest early pace suits their patient style perfectly.

Bobbarelli may get too easy a lead early and have enough left to resist late challenges despite seeking first rules win
Western Soldier's jumping under pressure as he was unseated in March and needs to negotiate hurdles cleanly from behind
Play Pretend's fluency over hurdles after lacking rhythm when beaten 36 lengths last time out at Taunton
Strong As Steel and Alex The Great both represent Tony Carroll but both have pulled up recently and may not complete

races.paceDynamic: Politacus will lead from the start with October Hill and Shesonnet likely tracking in prominent positions, creating a sustainable gallop over this stamina test. The pace should be genuine but not frantic given the distance and lack of natural speed horses. This will develop into a staying test from 3f out where stamina and tactical positioning matter most. This race shape clearly favours prominent runners who can stay close to the pace and hold-up horses with proven stamina who can finish strongly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If October Hill or Kom Tu Voudras can sit second/third and maintain position turning for home
scenarios.body: The sustainable pace allows prominent runners to stay in touch without over-racing, then kick clear when the leaders tire. These horses get first run on the field and the stamina test suits their profiles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong and the leaders come back significantly in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Belle Le Grand and Hello Cello can use their superior finishing speed to sweep past tired leaders. The longer distance gives them time to recover lost ground and Harry Skelton's tactical nous on Belle Le Grand proves decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wire-to-Wire Success
scenarios.trigger: If Politacus gets an uncontested lead and the pace becomes too slow for closers to make up ground
scenarios.body: The front-runner maintains a rhythm that suits her stamina strengths and kicks clear from 2f out. Any prominent tracker who tries to go with her cracks under pressure, leaving her clear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is too slow and becomes a sprint finish where class tells
scenarios.body: The race becomes tactical and scrappy, favouring horses with the highest ratings who can quicken. Form and class override tactical positioning in a messy finish where several horses have chances.

All Inn Hand's early jumping and travelling to gauge if fitness issues from spring runs are resolved
